stories.delivered_paragraph: Apple has reportedly delayed its first smart glasses from an early-2027 target to a June 2027 unveiling, with sales expected by year-end, as it works on privacy safeguards and how to explain them. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple plans to stress on-device processing and no facial recognition, while avoiding use of customer recordings to train AI. The approach would distinguish Apple from criticism of camera-equipped Meta glasses and test whether privacy can be a selling point for wearable cameras.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A small but growing group of Democrats, including Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and California Rep. Ro Khanna, is reclaiming “America First” to oppose U.S. spending on foreign wars and prioritize domestic costs. Their rhetoric responds to President Donald Trump’s war with Iran alongside Israel, which Axios reports is also splitting the political right. The shift could make a slogan long associated with Trump a contested message in the 2026 midterms and 2028 presidential race.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A Democratic National Committee panel voted to begin the 2028 presidential primary in South Carolina, angering progressives who say the state’s electorate favors the party establishment over their candidates. Bernie Sanders lost South Carolina heavily in both 2016 and 2020, while he won Nevada’s 2020 contest; Nevada had competed for the first slot. The calendar fight adds to tensions between the party’s left wing and centrists already battling over candidate choices in 2026 primaries.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Israeli settlers set fire to two mosques and damaged cars and farmland in West Bank villages, Palestinian officials said, two days after clashes near Tal killed four Palestinians and two Israelis. Palestinian reports described vandalism, theft and hate graffiti, while Israel’s military said troops were sent to Qusra and police would investigate. The attacks deepen an already volatile cycle of settler-Palestinian violence in the occupied territory, where both sides blame the other for recent confrontations.

stories.delivered_paragraph: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged continued support for Ukraine before hosting President Volodymyr Zelensky, his first international visitor since taking office a week ago. Britain will share intellectual property for its tablet-sized Stone Cloak electronic-warfare system so Ukraine can manufacture it at scale; the Defence Ministry has already supplied thousands of the drone-protection jammers. The move expands Ukraine’s ability to counter drones while signaling that London intends to maintain military backing against Russia.

stories.delivered_paragraph: MLB contenders are weighing last-minute upgrades before the Aug. 3 trade deadline at 6 p.m. ET, with Detroit ace Tarik Skubal and Boston closer Aroldis Chapman among the biggest names being watched. Detroit’s recent surge has made a Skubal deal less certain, while several playoff hopefuls, including the Dodgers, Yankees and Phillies, could buy. The deadline will help determine which teams strengthen their October chances and which hold onto stars for a postseason push.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Charli xcx released a $4.99 digital deluxe edition of “Music, Fashion, Film” on iTunes, making three previously physical-only B-sides available for purchase on July 26. The package adds “I Keep On Thinking Bout You Every Single Day and Night,” “Playboy Bunny” and “If You Take the Music Then What Has She Got?” plus videos to the album’s 11 tracks. It reverses her earlier suggestion that the songs would not reach streaming, though the release is currently an iTunes download.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Tadej Pogacar won his fifth Tour de France, tying the record held by Eddy Merckx, Miguel Indurain, Bernard Hinault and Jacques Anquetil. The 27-year-old Slovenian took the yellow jersey on stage six and finished 6 minutes 26 seconds ahead after holding it for the final 15 stages. Pogacar is the youngest five-time winner, putting him within reach of becoming the race’s sole record holder if he continues competing at this level.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Verge argues that John De Hart’s “Champagne and Bullets,” also released as “GetEven” and “Road to Revenge,” deserves a place alongside cult “so bad it’s good” films such as “The Room” and “Troll 2.” De Hart wrote, directed and starred in the low-budget film, even performing the awkward “Shimmy Slide” musical number. The review frames its incoherent dialogue and amateurish ambition as the qualities that make it a rewarding outsider-cinema curiosity for bad-movie fans.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige said director Ryan Coogler selected David Jonsson as the next Black Panther after a secret meeting roughly six weeks before the studio had planned to start its casting search. Coogler, then working on “Sinners,” told Feige Jonsson was “the guy” after meeting him, prompting Feige to approve the choice. The account confirms the creative team has identified its new lead for “Black Panther 3,” though no release timetable was provided.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Apple will report earnings in the busiest week of the summer season, while the Federal Reserve’s July policy meeting adds another potential market catalyst. Investors will focus on whether the largest technology companies can sustain growth expectations after Alphabet’s results and amid renewed Middle East tensions that have lifted oil prices. The combination matters because Big Tech results and Fed guidance can quickly reset expectations for corporate profits, interest rates and the broader stock market.

stories.delivered_paragraph: U.S. stock-index futures rose and oil prices fell Sunday after the United States and Iran paused attacks, easing investors’ immediate fears of a broader disruption to energy supplies. The relief rally comes before a crowded week featuring the Federal Reserve’s policy meeting and earnings from major technology companies. Markets remain sensitive to whether the fighting pause holds, because renewed conflict could reverse the drop in oil and complicate the outlook for inflation and interest rates.
